scope.reviewed: All Day02–60 original dialogues and quizzes, Day01 original rows/UI, the remade Day01 selection, all 300 English guide lines and the three modified safety turns in all five locales.
scope.not_claimed: Quiz evidence selection is owned by the lesson authors and independent curriculum review; this review covers factual meaning, not replay timing.

method.discovery: Official pages and search-service URL discovery; cited page content re-fetched directly with required User-Agent.
method.source_date_policy: Current official pages fetched on checked_date; no search snippet used as sole claim evidence.
method.jurisdiction_policy: Sources substantiate conditional practical advice, not worldwide laws or airline-independent numeric limits.
method.approval_policy: This report is factual evidence only; it is not a production or publishing approval.

turns: all fictional dialogue, quiz answers, numbers and place descriptions
claims.claim: Flight numbers, gates, counters, terminal layouts, distances, fares, airline names, meal choices, hotel names and personal itineraries are listening examples.
claims.support: These scripts describe invented conversations rather than named real airport operating arrangements. Do not fact-check invented flight842 or gateB32 against a live timetable.
claims.action: Label every episode and upload description as a fictional language-learning scenario; never represent example amounts or permissions as a current universal policy.
claims.suggested_wording: These are fictional listening scenarios. Check your airline, airport and destination's current requirements for your own journey.

claims.claim: Baggage allowances and gate-checking depend on the booking, airline, aircraft and capacity.
claims.quote: Baggage allowances and conditions of carriage remain airline specific.
claims.support: IATA explicitly varies allowances and permits cabin baggage to be moved to the hold when cabin capacity is exceeded. The lesson's three-kilogram excess is a fictional booking result, not a standard allowance.
claims.action: Retain conditional allowance wording; do not add an unsupported universal weight limit.

claims.claim: Keep the baggage receipt; remove old routing tags so scanners use the current tag.
claims.quote: Your newest baggage tag is the one that tells the system where your bag needs to go.
claims.support: Gatwick advises removing previous tags and stickers. Lufthansa advises retaining the boarding pass and baggage receipt. Photographing a receipt is optional practical advice, not a substitute for keeping the original.
claims.action: No factual change required.

claims.claim: Screening instructions can differ by checkpoint; follow staff and lane-specific procedures.
claims.quote: The rules for carrying liquids in your hand luggage depend on the airport.
claims.support: GOV.UK describes different liquid rules among airports. Heathrow currently permits large electrical items to stay inside cabin bags at its connection checks, demonstrating why the script's 'For this lane' qualifier matters.
claims.action: Preserve 'for this lane' and local-instruction language. Phone brightness, accessible chairs and particular screening outcomes are illustrative staff interactions, not guaranteed services or documentary requirements.

claims.claim: Declare liquid medicine to screening staff and have supporting prescription information available; needed medicines should remain accessible.
claims.quote: Airport staff might need to open the containers to screen the liquids at the security point.
claims.support: GOV.UK allows essential medicines subject to checks and, in specified cases, prescription proof. BA advises carrying medication needed during the flight in hand baggage. These examples do not establish destination import permission.
claims.action: No global medication exemption or permission to import controlled medicines is claimed; retain officer-directed wording.

claims.claim: Board according to the assigned group and crew instructions; assistance and stroller arrangements require confirmation.
claims.quote: Please be at the gate on time, ready to board the aircraft when your group is called.
claims.support: BA and American describe boarding groups and assistance procedures that differ. The example's printed group location, family eligibility and stroller return point are not asserted to apply to every airline.
claims.action: Do not turn fictional first-group examples into a universal boarding order.

claims.claim: Boarding/gate closure occurs before departure; departure time is not the latest gate-arrival time.
claims.quote: You will not be allowed to board once the doors close.
claims.support: American publishes distinct boarding and departure cutoffs. The lesson appropriately teaches the distinction without copying that airline's numeric cutoff to all flights.
claims.action: No factual change required.

claims.claim: A power bank must be removed before the bag is checked at the gate and kept in permitted cabin storage.
claims.quote: all spare lithium batteries and power banks must be removed from the bag
claims.support: FAA requires cabin carriage of spare lithium batteries/power banks, protected against short circuit; carriers may apply additional limits. Merely asking about battery rules under-specifies the action in a gate-check scenario.
claims.original_wording: Tell the agent before handing over the bag. They will explain the applicable battery rules.
claims.suggested_wording: Remove it before the bag is checked. Ask the agent how to carry it safely in the cabin.
claims.action: Applied English and four translations match the reviewed meaning; see exact production source/content hashes.

claims.claim: Underseat stowage depends on the seat's permitted storage configuration, restraint and clear aisle.
claims.quote: each item carried in a cabin should be stowed only in a location that is capable of restraining it
claims.support: CAA specifies restraints for underseat stowage; IATA notes restrictions such as exit rows and lack of a seat in front. Physical fit alone does not establish permission.
claims.original_wording: Yes, if it fits fully underneath and does not block the aisle.
claims.suggested_wording: Yes, if the crew permits it and it fits fully under the seat without blocking the aisle.
claims.action: Applied English and four translations match the reviewed meaning; see exact production source/content hashes.

claims.claim: Listen to the safety demonstration, read the aircraft's card, locate exits in both directions and ask crew if unclear.
claims.quote: Familiarise yourself with your nearest exit, which may be behind you.
claims.support: CAA says exit/equipment positions vary by aircraft and the nearest exit may be behind the passenger. A card in the seat pocket is the fictional aircraft's placement.
claims.action: No factual change required; retain aircraft-specific qualification.

claims.claim: On the demonstrated lift-tab buckle, lift to release; fasten and pull the loose strap to tighten.
claims.quote: To tighten the belt, pull the free end until it fits comfortably.
claims.support: Air Cambodia's official briefing separately describes fastening, tightening and lifting the metal tab to unfasten. Original wording conflates releasing with subsequent fit adjustment.
claims.original_wording: Lift the metal buckle to release it, then pull the strap to adjust the fit.
claims.suggested_wording: Lift the metal buckle to release it. To tighten it, fasten it and pull the loose end of the strap.
claims.action: Applied English and four translations match the reviewed meaning; see exact production source/content hashes.

claims.claim: Follow seat-belt signs and crew directions; keep the belt fastened while seated, and avoid accessing bins during turbulence.
claims.quote: Whenever the seat belt sign is illuminated during flight
claims.support: FAA and CAA support seated belt use. JAL distinguishes unexpected severe turbulence when already away from a seat: secure oneself immediately. Day40 is a captain's advance warning, not permission to walk during an already violent encounter.
claims.action: Preserve crew-led context. Do not expand into instructions to traverse the cabin during severe turbulence. Meal service suspension is conditional, not a guaranteed procedure.

claims.claim: Stow larger devices, use permitted connectivity settings and report an overheating device immediately.
claims.quote: Passengers should notify flight crew immediately if their lithium battery or device is overheating, expanding, smoking or burning.
claims.support: CAA says to follow crew instructions for flight mode/connectivity. FAA explicitly requires immediate reporting of hazardous device behaviour. Stowage and landing configuration follow the aircraft crew.
claims.action: No universal Wi-Fi permission or automatic post-touchdown permission is claimed.

claims.claim: If a phone falls into a seat mechanism, do not move the seat; ask cabin crew for help.
claims.quote: If your phone becomes lost inflight, do not move the seat; contact a crew member immediately!
claims.support: TTCAA's official passenger safety guidance directly supports the lesson's two actions.
claims.action: No factual change required.

claims.claim: Ask about ingredients, do not assume an allergen-free cabin/meal, read available labels and alert crew if unwell.
claims.quote: We cannot guarantee an allergen-free environment while travelling with us.
claims.support: BA provides ingredient information but declines an allergen-free guarantee and advises serious-allergy passengers to discuss risks with their doctor and notify crew. Meal availability and package ingredients in the lesson are fictional.
claims.action: No medical treatment instructions are given. Reading a label does not guarantee safety; retain the explicit medical-advice/cross-contact qualification.

claims.claim: Call crew promptly when someone is unwell, report symptoms/known conditions and the location of prescribed medication, and follow crew directions.
claims.support: Official cabin guidance directs passengers to crew for safety and medical-support communication. The lesson does not diagnose dizziness or breathing trouble and does not prescribe, dose or tell another passenger to administer medicine.
claims.action: Keep this as help-seeking language, not a self-treatment protocol.

claims.claim: Transfer routing and baggage collection depend on itinerary/local process; a final-destination bag tag does not always avoid reclaim/recheck.
claims.quote: Check with your airline if you’re not sure.
claims.support: Heathrow distinguishes through connections from separately booked journeys requiring reclaim and check-in. DOT describes first international entry into the U.S. as a place a traveller may need to pick up and recheck baggage. Neither pattern is universal.
claims.action: Day41's 'Transfers' route is staff direction for that fictional through connection, not a worldwide rule; preserve local itinerary checks in teaching recap.

claims.claim: For a sealed duty-free liquid, show the receipt and sealed security bag; let screening staff direct opening and applicability.
claims.support: GOV.UK describes sealed security bags with visible receipts and possible staff opening for screening. Transit rules vary, so the script correctly does not promise universal acceptance.
claims.action: Do not say a sealed bag alone guarantees transfer security acceptance.

claims.claim: Contact the airline about disruption options; available seats, assistance and baggage arrangements depend on the journey and circumstances.
claims.quote: What you are entitled to depends on many factors.
claims.support: Canada's official consumer authority explains how circumstances affect rebooking/refunds/support and recommends asking the carrier and retaining documentation. Local law may require rights beyond the carrier's policy; the scripts neither waive rights nor promise specific compensation.
claims.action: Retain conditional language. Do not interpret 'check airline policy' as allowing the airline to override legal rights.

claims.claim: Border procedures and documents depend on destination/nationality; answer questions accurately and present actual travel details.
claims.quote: You may be asked questions at the UK border about your eligibility and the activities you plan to do.
claims.support: GOV.UK explains eligibility/document checks. Tourism, conference invitations, hotel bookings and onward tickets are example answers, not sufficient proof of admission or an instruction to misstate purpose. Stay lengths and dates in the conversations are fictional.
claims.action: No visa advice is implied. Don't tell learners to repeat fictional facts as their own or imply these phrases guarantee entry.

claims.claim: Report delayed/damaged baggage promptly, keep identifying documents/report numbers, describe the bag and confirm delivery details.
claims.quote: Passengers should file a baggage claim with their airline as soon as possible.
claims.support: DOT supports prompt claims and tracing; IATA says to file a missing-bag report before leaving reclaim. Delayed does not automatically mean permanently lost. Damage remedies/claim limits depend on applicable rules; direct replacement and delivery timing are not guaranteed. BA distinguishes the report reference from the original bag receipt and advises keeping damaged baggage; Lufthansa supports updating delivery addresses and contact details.
claims.action: No fixed reporting deadline, lost-bag deadline or compensation amount is taught. Retain the conditional delivery/replacement wording.

claims.claim: Clarify declaration requirements with customs and accurately disclose relevant goods, including gifts carried for someone else.
claims.quote: You and your baggage can be checked for anything that must be declared.
claims.support: Official customs guidance requires declaration of specified goods and allows goods inspection. The lesson does not claim every gift is prohibited or exempt and never guarantees a sealed package can be imported.
claims.action: Retain destination-specific requirements; no monetary threshold or food-import allowance is asserted.

claims.claim: Use an airport's designated taxi rank and confirm the destination/fare arrangement; assistance can help find a suitable vehicle.
claims.support: Heathrow documents licensed taxis at designated terminal ranks. Door Three, local attendants and luggage capacity are invented dialogue details. This source does not prove every airport has the same taxi layout or fare method.
claims.action: No factual change required.

supplemental_reviews.scope: Read the four new English dialogue turns and all sixteen corresponding translated strings for factual meaning; compare preserved fourteen turns, three quizzes/evidence IDs, guides, titles, claims and sources. Re-read corrected adaptation note. Canonical integration changes only status from the actually reviewed proposal.
supplemental_reviews.findings: The fictional Sunrise Airlines sign and queue in Zone C, and fictional Maple Airlines queue beside the stairs, are local role-play details. Confirming with these staff is not presented as a universal airport policy. No new external factual claim or required correction.

supplemental_brief_review.findings: Read parseable A/B outline options and exact Q1 worked example. A matches current per-dialogue practice; B is explicitly an alternative requiring reorder. Q1 question, Zone B/D/C options, B01/B02 evidence, choose with four-second line pause, B/Zone D answer and explanation match generated entries. This is text/order review, not audio timing.
